analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift (new), NetworkFrameworkCloseCodeTests.swift (new), and the MockCoordinator.swift helper (modified). None of them changes production code, so there is no change to key custody, attestation, encryption, authorization, billing or data exposure.

MockCoordinator.dropActiveWebSocket (head lines 445-456) now takes a closeCode (default 1001) and a reason (default "mock dropping"). Existing callers keep the old behavior. The helper binds only to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and is test-only, so it adds no new attack surface.

The tests exercise the reconnect policy and Network.framework close-code parsing. Both are consumed by production CoordinatorClient code that is outside this batch. These are the policy rows:
- A session open for 60 s or more resets the backoff.
- Close code 1012 gives a 0-1 s wait with no backoff growth.
- Every other end keeps the existing backoff.

The security-relevant property is availability on the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider WebSocket. The coordinator is trusted, so a 1012 shortcut is a small reconnect-storm risk at most. Unreviewed integration questions: whether the production policy bounds a rapid 1012 loop (the tests show that 1012 never grows the backoff, so repeated 1012 closes could cause a tight 0-1 s reconnect loop), and whether a reconnect still re-runs full registration and attestation (TB-009/TB-011 authorization is per connection). The production CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorClient sources were not supplied, so no conclusion about them is drawn. No threat-model change is needed for these test-only edits.
